seoTitle: How to Build a Wix Website From a Blank Template
metaDescription: Start a Wix site from a genuinely blank canvas instead of a pre-built template: adding sections, editing content, building extra pages, and publishing.
intro: Starting from a blank Wix canvas means every section, every page, and every piece of navigation is something you place on purpose, instead of trimming down someone else's design. It takes longer than picking a pre-built template, but it's the right route when your layout doesn't fit any of Wix's presets. This guide covers creating the site, adding your first section, and building out extra pages such as an About page from nothing.

steps.heading: Start a new site and pick the blank option
steps.body: Every Wix site you own lives on the Sites dashboard, reachable from My Sites in the top navigation. Click Create New Site to start fresh. Wix now usually asks what the site is for first and offers an AI-assisted setup that generates a starting layout from a short description; if you want a truly empty canvas, skip that chat and go to the template gallery instead, where Blank Template is still a listed option alongside the themed designs. Picking it drops you into the editor with nothing on the page.

image.caption: The Wix Sites dashboard, listing every site in the account with an option to create a new one.

steps.heading: Open the editor and add your first section
steps.body: With a blank page open in the editor, click Add Section. Wix doesn't leave you positioning individual elements from zero: the panel organizes pre-structured layouts by purpose, including Welcome, About, Team, and Contact, so you're choosing a structural starting point for each part of the page. Picking one of these still counts as building from scratch, since the page itself started empty.

image.caption: The Add Section panel, offering pre-structured layouts like Welcome, About, and Team to drop onto an otherwise empty page.

steps.heading: Drop the section onto the canvas and edit the content
steps.body: Once you pick a layout, it lands on the page with placeholder text and imagery in place: a heading like "Welcome," a short description, and a background image. Double-click any text box to edit it directly. The Add Section button stays visible below your last section so you can keep stacking new ones as the page grows downward.

image.caption: A Welcome section placed on the canvas, with its placeholder heading and description ready to be edited.

steps.heading: Add and build out additional pages
steps.body: A single Home page rarely covers a real site, so open Pages & Menu in the left sidebar to add more. From there, click Add Page: Wix offers page templates sorted by purpose (About, Services, Contact, and others), or you can click +Blank Page at the top to skip them and start that page empty too. A new page is added to your site menu automatically, and you build it the same way you built Home, one section at a time, with content suited to that page's purpose. Keeping spacing and typography consistent between pages is what makes a hand-built site read as intentional instead of assembled piecemeal.

image.caption: The Pages & Menu panel, listing Home, About, Portfolio, and Book Online as separate pages with their own navigation entries.

steps.heading: Check mobile view before publishing
steps.body: Toggle the mobile view icon near the top of the editor to see how sections reflow on a phone-sized screen. A layout built section by section doesn't inherit the tested responsive behavior of a pre-made template, so review every page in mobile view specifically. Text that looks fine on desktop can crowd or overlap once the viewport narrows, and this is the fastest way to catch that before visitors do.

steps.heading: Preview and publish
steps.body: Click Preview to interact with the site as a visitor would, checking that navigation links move between pages correctly and that nothing looks unfinished. When it holds up, click Publish. You can always jump back into the editor from the Sites dashboard to keep adding pages or sections later.

troubleshooting.problem: A new page opens with a layout you didn't ask for
troubleshooting.cause: Add Page in Pages & Menu defaults to a gallery of pre-built page templates sorted by category.
troubleshooting.fix: Click +Blank Page at the top of that gallery to skip the templates and start the page empty, the same way you started Home.

troubleshooting.problem: Pages look inconsistent once you've built a few of them
troubleshooting.cause: Building every page independently, section by section, makes it easy for fonts, colors, and spacing to drift from page to page.
troubleshooting.fix: Reuse the same section categories where the content is similar, and check your site's theme settings (fonts and colors) rather than styling each new text box from scratch.

troubleshooting.problem: The site looks fine on desktop but broken on mobile
troubleshooting.cause: A hand-built layout has no template to inherit tested responsive behavior from, so overlapping text and crowded sections only show up once the viewport narrows.
troubleshooting.fix: Toggle mobile view on every page before publishing, not just Home, and adjust spacing there directly.

faq.question: Is building from a blank template harder than using a pre-made one?
faq.answer: It takes more manual layout work since you're placing every section yourself, but the Add Section panel still offers pre-structured layouts for common needs, so you're not positioning individual elements from zero.

faq.question: Does Wix still let me skip the AI setup and start truly blank?
faq.answer: Yes. Wix's newer site-creation flow leads with an AI-assisted chat by default, but the template gallery still lists a Blank Template option, and choosing it opens the standard editor with an empty page.

faq.question: How do I make sure my blank layout looks good on mobile?
faq.answer: Toggle the mobile view icon in the editor and review every page individually. A hand-built layout doesn't inherit the tested responsive behavior a pre-made template ships with.

faq.question: Do I need to build navigation manually on a blank site?
faq.answer: No. Adding a page through Pages & Menu adds it to your site menu automatically, so basic navigation is handled as you create pages.

Panel names and the page-adding flow were re-checked against Wix's Help Center in September 2026, which corrected this guide's earlier "Site Pages and Menu" label to Wix's actual current panel name, Pages & Menu, and added the note that new sites now typically start with an AI setup prompt rather than landing straight in a blank editor.
